observations.content:
Summary: GPT-3, as explained in the paper by Brown et al. 2020, has 175 billion parameters. The model is built on GPT-2's design and is about 117 times larger. The paper estimates that generating one token with the 175B model costs the forward-pass share. The model has 96 layers, each with four d×d attention matrices and two feed-forward matrices of size d×4d, contributing to the total parameter count. The token embedding and position embedding add to the total, resulting in approximately 174.6 billion parameters. Wikipedia confirms that GPT-3 has 175 billion parameters, each with 16-bit precision, requiring 350GB of storage.

[1] GPT-3 explained — Language Models Are Few-Shot Learners
    https://intuitivepapers.ai/gpt-3
    GPT-3 is a next-token predictor built on GPT-2's design and about 117 times larger. The paper never trains it on a task. It writes a few solved examples into the prompt, reads what the model writes next, and measures how well that works at eight model sizes from 125 million to 175 billion parameters.

The same rule gives 2.60 PF-days for the 125M model, and it ignores the attention operation itself, which the paper estimates at under 10% of the total for these models. Generating one token with the 175B model costs the forward-pass share, 2 [...] The 175B row is enough to recover the parameter count. Each layer has four d×d attention matrices (query, key, value, output) and two feed-forward matrices of size d×4d, so about 12d2 weights. With d=12,288 and 96 layers:
